doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Hino's Day Dreams and Hino leaving the quintet
summary: On Hino's big-budget Japanese session, Liebman recalls Hino leaving his quintet without being able to say so.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Interesting. Here’s a big date with Hino for Flying Disc for Japan with a string section, and Marvin Stamm, all the studio heavies of the time.
That is a Hino production, production date that I probably just came and overdubbed.
It’s Japan. That’s Hino. That is what? ’80, ’81?

Because that is when Hino started to get busy with his career in Japan, and that’s when I had to get Kenny Kirkland for that group. He left me. We had – I remember I was very upset. He didn’t leave me, but he had to do it. But he couldn’t talk to me about it. I’ll never forget it. I learned something. He didn’t tell me. He didn’t come or something. I confronted him. I said, “Hino . . . .” He said, “Japanese, we can’t face. We don’t confront.” “Hino, you’re a bro. You’re a brother, man.” He says, “Dave, I just couldn’t tell you.”
It’s like Coltrane when he had to get a piano player and get Elvin.
He was honest. I can’t explain it, but he was honest, at least.
Okay. I’ve talked about the John McNeil dates.
See, I can remember every one – almost every one.
